newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bankgesellschaft seeks to oust chairman - report.
newsitem.headline: Bankgesellschaft seeks to oust chairman - report.

text.p: Germany's Bankgesellschaft Berlin is seeking the resignation of supervisory board chairman Edzard Reuter after the group was forced into huge bad debt provisions for 1996, a report in Der Spiegel magazine said on Sunday.

The Spiegel report, due to be published on Monday, said that Bankgesellschaft held Reuter and chief executive Wolfgang Steinriede, who has resigned his post and leaves at the end of this year, responsible for the huge provisions.
There was no one available for comment at Bankgesellschaft.

In November, the group said it would would set aside 2.2 billion marks of provisions in its 1996 balance sheet. To date 60 percent of the bank's senior management has been changed, and the board was waiting for Reuter's resignation, the Spiegel report said.
The group's other chief executive, Hubertus Moser, will also give up his position at the end of the year. The chief executive designate, Wolfgang Rupf, will take over from January 1.

Bankgesellschaft, formed in 1994 through the merging of three Berlin banking groups, has been constantly dogged by problems due to high risk provisions and costs linked to internal restructuring measures.
The city-state of Berlin holds more than 50 percent of the group.
